<!--
RENUMBERED 2026-08-10: this figure is now FIGURE 7. It was Figure 6 until the tau_int decision
panel was promoted into the body as Figure 5 and the corner figure became Figure 6. The archive
directory name (archive/figure_6_superseded_20260731) keeps its old number on purpose: it is dated.

WHAT THIS IS. One plane, N_ch x instrumental noise, partitioned by boundaries into the regimes that
decide what a macroscopic recording can support. Unlike every other figure in this set it is NOT a
heatmap: the content is the boundaries, so the cells are the input and the lines are the output.

THE ENCODING (Luciano, 2026-07-26) — one visual channel per meaning, no exceptions:

    COLOUR    = the PARAMETER the line is about:  k_on, k_off, i (unitary conductance), N_ch
    LINE TYPE = WHAT is being asked about it:
        solid   "can it be measured at all"  -> distortion-corrected SE crosses a factor 2
        dotted  "is ILSE's error bar honest"  -> ILSE's information distortion crosses 1.15
        dashed  "is IR's own error bar honest" -> IR's information distortion crosses 1.15
                 (this one is the macro/micro floor: below it the Gaussian closure is misspecified)
    RIBBON    = the same boundary swept over the sampling interval, Delta.k_off = 0.01 to 1.
                The heavy line is the reference Delta.k_off = 0.1. So the ribbon is not an error
                bar, it is "where your own sampling rate puts the boundary".

WHERE THE SE FAMILY COMES FROM, and why it is mixed: the RATES from ILSE, the AMPLITUDE from IR.
"Where does this parameter die" is a property of the experiment, so in principle it should be judged
by the best available method — but measured, IR and ILSE rate SEs agree to a few percent at N_ch >= 100
(the only gap is N_ch 10, where ILSE loses a factor 1.9 on k_on, and there both are already past the
threshold), while ILSE is the one with the high-noise coverage: at N_ch 1e4 IR stops at noise 1e5 and
ILSE runs to 1e7, so an IR-sourced rate boundary simply vanishes off the right of the plot. The
amplitude pair must come from IR, because ILSE holds unitary_current Fixed and never estimates i at
all — which is the structural point of the figure, not a coverage accident.

THE REGIONS, bottom to top at fixed N_ch:
    0  below the dashed line: the Gaussian closure itself fails. Labelled "closure fails", NOT
       "use micro": micro is not measured in this paper.
    1  i and N_ch both resolved AND ILSE's error bar wrong  -> IR buys two things
    2  amplitude gone, rates alive, ILSE still wrong        -> IR buys one thing (an honest CI)
    3  ILSE's error bar honest and rates alive              -> IR buys nothing, ILSE is par
    4  above the solid k_on line: nothing useful left
  The 2x2 cell "amplitude alive AND ILSE honest" is EMPTY at every measured cell, which is what makes
  these an ordered ladder rather than a table.

WHY k_on IS THE BINDING RATE: SE(k_on) ~ 3.1 x SE(k_off) everywhere measured, for both methods. One
concentration jump, so k_off is read twice (pulse rate and washout) while k_on comes only from their
difference. Region 4 therefore opens on k_on, ~1 decade of noise below where k_off alone would die,
and both lines are drawn so the reader can pick the criterion that matches what they need.

TRAPS, none of them re-derivable from the plot:
 - param_index is a POSITION IN THE FREE PARAMETER VECTOR, so the map differs by algorithm:
     macro: 0 on, 1 off, 2 unitary_current, 3 Current_Noise, 4 Current_Baseline, 5 Num_ch_mean
     ILSE  : 0 on, 1 off, 2 Current_Baseline, 3 Num_ch_mean   (the two Fixed ones are absent)
   A single global PIDX silently drops ILSE from anything keyed on index 5 and mislabels index 3.
 - the y axis is the RAW noise label, and current_noise = label/1000. Never divide it by N_ch: the
   diagonal boundaries are the finding, and dividing flattens them by construction.
 - N_ch is NOT capped to four columns. IR has runs at 5/20/50/200/500/2000/5000 and the closure floor
   is the best-sampled boundary in N_ch; with four columns its crossing (N_ch ~ 70-150) is invisible.
   Those extra columns are LOW-NOISE runs, so they help the floor and not the high-noise boundaries.
 - everything comes from battery_pool_G (theta_pool anchor), so the figure is internally consistent
   on one anchor. Bias (battery_sim_G) is not on this figure.

MEASURED, at Delta.k_off = 0.1 (the render log prints all of it):
  slopes, d log10 noise / d log10 N_ch:  ILSE-honest 1.01 (k_off) and 1.03 (N_ch), i.e. N_ch-independent
  in r = noise/N_ch;  SE(i) 1.11;  SE(N_ch) 1.61;  SE(k_off) 2.24 and SE(k_on) 2.21;  closure floor
  -0.56, NEGATIVE — instrumental noise gaussianises the emission, so it HELPS the closure while
  hurting everything else. That sign contrast is the second non-obvious thing in the figure.
  region 3 (ILSE is par) OPENS at N_ch 120 to 1368, the range being the strict-vs-loose criterion.
  the map CLOSES from below at N_ch 3 to 9, EXTRAPOLATED — exactly where the planned N_ch 2 and 5
  runs would land, which is the cheapest run this figure asks for.
  the loose criterion moves the SE boundaries up by a factor 9 (i, N_ch) to 19-21 (the rates) in
  noise, and the distortion boundaries down by a factor 2-3. That is why the vertices are ranges.
-->

```{r data}
DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7")
DIST <- "Probit_statistics_Likelihood_Gaussian_Information_Distortion"
SEC  <- "Probit_statistics_Gaussian_Distortion_Corrected_Covariance"
DREF <- 0.1                       # reference interval, in units of tau = 1/k_off
DRNG <- c(0.01, 1)                # interval range spanned by the ribbons

read_algo <- function(pat, algo, idx) {
  fs <- list.files(DATA_DIRS, pattern = pat, full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(fs)) stop("figure_7: no files for ", algo)
  map_dfr(fs, function(p) read.csv(p, skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    filter(component_path %in% c(DIST, SEC), statistic == "value", probit == "mean",
           param_index == param_col, param_index %in% idx) %>%
    transmute(algo = algo, nch = Num_ch, noise = noise_in_conductance_tau, D = interval_in_tau,
              what = ifelse(component_path == DIST, "dist", "var"),
              par = names(idx)[match(param_index, idx)], v = value)) %>% distinct()
}
IR  <- read_algo("^figure_3_G_nch_[0-9]+_nsim_10000_macro_IR_noise_[0-9.eE+]+_battery_pool_G\\.csv$",
                 "IR",  c(kon = 0, koff = 1, i = 2, Nch = 5))
# RELABELLED 2026-08-11 (Luciano): this pattern matches `nonlinearsqr`, which is the
# INTERVAL-AVERAGED least-squares arm, ILSE (figure_4.Rmd:329-330; the data-file tokens are crossed
# on purpose, see figure_1.Rmd). The un-averaged arm is `nonlinearsqr_g` and is NOT read here. The
# label said ILSE and the classical arm of this map is therefore ILSE throughout.
ILSE <- read_algo("^figure_3_LSE_nch_[0-9]+_nsim_10000_nonlinearsqr_noise_[0-9.eE+]+_battery_pool_G\\.csv$",
                 "ILSE", c(kon = 0, koff = 1, Nch = 3))

# THE SECOND CLASSICAL ARM, added 2026-08-26. Until now the record said nothing about why this map
# uses ILSE rather than the un-averaged arm, and "the boundaries would not move" was asserted
# nowhere and established nowhere (04_results.tex, note retracted 2026-08-12). It is now measured.
# The un-averaged arm is `nonlinearsqr_g` (averaging = 0, the mean is the bare conductance half an
# interval in, NR's mean model) and it landed in ../data/a202e03 after this map was built: 30 cells
# on the Gaussian lane, N_ch 10 to 10^4 and noise 0.1 to 1e7, the same coverage the map needs, with
# the same param_index layout. It is read from its own directory list so that the DRAWN map keeps
# reading exactly the three frozen directories and cannot move: a202e03 holds zero files matching
# either pattern above, checked, so this is additive by construction.
DATA_DIRS_XARM <- c(DATA_DIRS, "../data/a202e03")
LSE <- local({
  fs <- list.files(DATA_DIRS_XARM,
        pattern = "^figure_3_LSE_nch_[0-9]+_nsim_10000_nonlinearsqr_g_noise_[0-9.eE+]+_battery_pool_G\\.csv$",
        full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(fs)) NULL else map_dfr(fs, function(p) read.csv(p, skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    filter(component_path %in% c(DIST, SEC), statistic == "value", probit == "mean",
           param_index == param_col, param_index %in% c(kon = 0, koff = 1, Nch = 3)) %>%
    transmute(algo = "LSE", nch = Num_ch, noise = noise_in_conductance_tau, D = interval_in_tau,
              what = ifelse(component_path == DIST, "dist", "var"),
              par = c("kon", "koff", NA, "Nch")[param_index + 1], v = value)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(par)) %>% distinct()
})

cat("figure_7: noise levels on disk, per algorithm and N_ch\n")
print(as.data.frame(bind_rows(IR, ILSE) %>% distinct(algo, nch, noise) %>% count(algo, nch) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = algo, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)), row.names = FALSE)

# one row per (question, parameter, nch, D, noise). SEs are already in log10 units; the distortion is
# two-sided (IR under-disperses N_ch where it over-disperses k_off), hence abs(log()).
MET <- bind_rows(
  ILSE %>% filter(what == "var", par %in% c("kon", "koff")) %>%
          transmute(q = "se",    par, nch, D, noise, m = sqrt(pmax(v, 0))),
  IR  %>% filter(what == "var", par %in% c("i", "Nch")) %>%
          transmute(q = "se",    par, nch, D, noise, m = sqrt(pmax(v, 0))),
  ILSE %>% filter(what == "dist") %>% transmute(q = "lse",   par, nch, D, noise, m = abs(log(v))),
  IR  %>% filter(what == "dist") %>% transmute(q = "floor", par, nch, D, noise, m = abs(log(v))))

# thresholds and drawing rules, per question
QQ <- tribble(
  ~q,      ~t1,       ~t2,      ~rising, ~lty,   ~qlab,
  "se",    0.3,       1.0,      TRUE,    "solid","solid: parameter no longer measurable (SE > factor 2)",
  "lse",   log(1.15), log(1.3), FALSE,   "12",   "dotted: ILSE's reported error bar becomes honest (distortion < 1.15)",
  "floor", log(1.15), log(1.3), FALSE,   "42",   "dashed: IR's OWN error bar is wrong -> Gaussian closure fails (distortion > 1.15)")
PARS <- c(kon = "k_on", koff = "k_off", i = "i  (unitary conductance)", Nch = "N_ch")
# which (question, parameter) pairs are drawn. k_on/k_off carry region 4; i and N_ch carry the
# amplitude boundary; the honesty questions are asked of k_off and N_ch (i is Fixed for ILSE).
DRAW <- tribble(~q, ~par,
  "se","kon", "se","koff", "se","i", "se","Nch",
  "lse","koff", "lse","Nch",
  "floor","koff", "floor","Nch")

cross1 <- function(x, y, t, rising) {          # interpolate in log10(noise); NA when off-grid
  o <- order(x); x <- x[o]; y <- y[o]; ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y); x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]
  if (length(x) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  s <- y - t
  if (all(s > 0) || all(s < 0)) return(NA_real_)
  k <- which(s[-length(s)] * s[-1] <= 0)
  if (!length(k)) return(NA_real_)
  i <- if (rising) k[1] else k[length(k)]
  x[i] + (t - y[i]) * (x[i + 1] - x[i]) / (y[i + 1] - y[i])
}
CR <- MET %>% inner_join(DRAW, by = c("q", "par")) %>% inner_join(QQ, by = "q") %>%
  group_by(q, par, qlab, lty, nch, D) %>%
  summarise(c1 = cross1(log10(noise), m, first(t1), first(rising)),
            c2 = cross1(log10(noise), m, first(t2), first(rising)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(lx = log10(nch), pf = factor(unname(PARS[par]), levels = unname(PARS)))

cat("\nfigure_7: boundary position (noise) at Delta.k_off =", DREF, ", strict criterion\n")
print(as.data.frame(CR %>% filter(D == DREF) %>% transmute(q, par, nch, noise = signif(10^c1, 3)) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = nch, values_from = noise, names_prefix = "N=")), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nfigure_7: fitted log-log slopes (d log10 noise / d log10 N_ch) at Delta.k_off =", DREF, "\n")
print(as.data.frame(CR %>% filter(D == DREF, is.finite(c1)) %>% group_by(q, par) %>% filter(n() >= 3) %>%
      summarise(slope = round(coef(lm(c1 ~ lx))[2], 2), n = n(), .groups = "drop")), row.names = FALSE)
# BEST ACHIEVABLE SE, minimised over the whole noise sweep. A parameter whose best is already past
# the threshold is NEVER measurable at that N_ch, at ANY noise -- which is why some boundary lines
# terminate. That is a physical statement, not missing data, so it is printed and annotated.
BEST <- MET %>% filter(q == "se", D == DREF) %>% group_by(par, nch) %>%
  summarise(best = min(m), .groups = "drop")
cat("\nfigure_7: best achievable SE over the whole noise sweep (> 0.3 = never measurable there)\n")
print(as.data.frame(BEST %>% pivot_wider(names_from = par, values_from = best) %>%
      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(.x, 3)))), row.names = FALSE)
NEVER <- BEST %>% group_by(par) %>% arrange(nch) %>%
  summarise(nch_min = if (min(best) > 0.3 || max(best) < 0.3) NA_real_ else
              10^approx(log10(best), log10(nch), xout = log10(0.3))$y, .groups = "drop")
cat("\nfigure_7: N_ch below which the parameter is UNREACHABLE at any noise\n")
print(as.data.frame(NEVER %>% mutate(nch_min = round(nch_min))), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nfigure_7: how far the loose criterion moves each boundary (median factor in noise)\n")
print(as.data.frame(CR %>% filter(D == DREF, is.finite(c1), is.finite(c2)) %>% group_by(q, par) %>%
      summarise(factor = round(median(10^(c2 - c1)), 2), n = n(), .groups = "drop")), row.names = FALSE)

# DOES THE CLASSICAL BOUNDARY MOVE IF THE OTHER LEAST-SQUARES ARM IS USED? Measured, not drawn.
# The dotted boundary is recomputed on the un-averaged arm with the same threshold and the same
# interpolation, and the two are reported side by side. It is deliberately NOT added to the plot:
# at the reference interval the two land within a factor of 1.4 of each other on a boundary that
# sweeps five decades, so a second dotted line would sit on top of the first and the figure would
# carry a fourth line code for no information. The number belongs in the text instead.
if (!is.null(LSE)) {
  XA <- LSE %>% filter(what == "dist", par %in% c("koff", "Nch")) %>%
        transmute(algo = "LSE", par, nch, D, noise, m = abs(log(v))) %>%
    bind_rows(ILSE %>% filter(what == "dist", par %in% c("koff", "Nch")) %>%
              transmute(algo = "ILSE", par, nch, D, noise, m = abs(log(v)))) %>%
    group_by(algo, par, nch, D) %>%
    summarise(c1 = cross1(log10(noise), m, log(1.15), FALSE), .groups = "drop")
  cat("\nfigure_7: the honesty boundary on BOTH least-squares arms (noise), Delta.k_off =", DREF, "\n")
  print(as.data.frame(XA %>% filter(D == DREF) %>%
        transmute(algo, par, nch, noise = signif(10^c1, 3)) %>%
        pivot_wider(names_from = nch, values_from = noise, names_prefix = "N=")), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nfigure_7: LSE / ILSE ratio of that boundary, and the fitted slopes\n")
  print(as.data.frame(XA %>% filter(D == DREF, is.finite(c1)) %>%
        pivot_wider(names_from = algo, values_from = c1) %>%
        mutate(ratio = signif(10^(LSE - ILSE), 3)) %>% select(par, nch, ratio)), row.names = FALSE)
  print(as.data.frame(XA %>% filter(D == DREF, is.finite(c1)) %>% mutate(lx = log10(nch)) %>%
        group_by(algo, par) %>% filter(n() >= 3) %>%
        summarise(slope = round(coef(lm(c1 ~ lx))[2], 3), n = n(), .groups = "drop")), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nfigure_7: the same over the ribbon range of Delta (", DRNG[1], "to", DRNG[2], "), in noise\n")
  print(as.data.frame(XA %>% filter(D >= DRNG[1], D <= DRNG[2], is.finite(c1)) %>%
        group_by(algo, par, nch) %>%
        summarise(lo = signif(10^min(c1), 3), hi = signif(10^max(c1), 3), .groups = "drop")),
        row.names = FALSE)
} else cat("\nfigure_7: the un-averaged least-squares arm is not on disk in", DATA_DIRS_XARM, "\n")
```

```{r geometry}
# the two vertices, each a RANGE bracketed by the strict and loose criteria on the SE(k_on) line
vx <- function(qa, pa, qb, pb, cb) {
  a <- CR %>% filter(q == qa, par == pa, D == DREF, is.finite(c1))
  b <- CR %>% filter(q == qb, par == pb, D == DREF, is.finite(.data[[cb]]))
  if (nrow(a) < 2 || nrow(b) < 2) return(NULL)
  fa <- coef(lm(c1 ~ lx, a)); fb <- coef(lm(as.formula(paste(cb, "~ lx")), b))
  x <- unname((fb[1] - fa[1]) / (fa[2] - fb[2]))
  tibble(lx = x, ly = unname(fa[1] + fa[2] * x))
}
v_open  <- list(vx("lse", "koff", "se", "kon", "c2"), vx("lse", "koff", "se", "kon", "c1"))
v_close <- list(vx("floor", "koff", "se", "kon", "c2"), vx("floor", "koff", "se", "kon", "c1"))
rng <- function(v) if (any(vapply(v, is.null, TRUE))) "NA" else
  sprintf("%.0f-%.0f", 10^min(v[[1]]$lx, v[[2]]$lx), 10^max(v[[1]]$lx, v[[2]]$lx))
cat("\nregion 3 (ILSE is par) OPENS at N_ch =", rng(v_open), "(range = the two criteria)\n")
cat("the map CLOSES from below at N_ch =", rng(v_close),
    "-- EXTRAPOLATED, this is what the N_ch 2 and 5 runs would pin\n")

PCOL <- c("k_on" = "#E69F00", "k_off" = "#009E73",
          "i  (unitary conductance)" = "#0072B2", "N_ch" = "#CC79A7")
# x reaches 3e7 so oocyte-scale preparations fit; the simulated span is marked on the plot
XLIM <- log10(c(2.5, 4e9)); YLIM <- log10(c(0.008, 5e7))
NOISE_MIN <- 0.05            # the lowest noise level anywhere in the sweep; below it we know nothing
xbrk <- log10(10^(1:9))
xlab <- c("10", expression(10^2), expression(10^3), expression(10^4), expression(10^5),
          expression(10^6), expression(10^7), expression(10^8), expression(10^9))
ybrk <- log10(10^(-2:7))
ylab <- c("0.01", "0.1", "1", "10", expression(10^2), expression(10^3), expression(10^4),
          expression(10^5), expression(10^6), expression(10^7))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6.6}
# ribbon = the boundary swept over the interval range; line = the reference interval
RIB <- CR %>% filter(D >= DRNG[1], D <= DRNG[2], is.finite(c1)) %>%
  group_by(q, par, pf, lty, nch, lx) %>%
  summarise(lo = min(c1), hi = max(c1), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>% filter(n >= 2)
LIN <- CR %>% filter(D == DREF, is.finite(c1)) %>% arrange(lx)
# A vertex is an N_ch RANGE, so it is drawn as a vertical strip. Deliberately NOT a line: line type
# already encodes the question, and a black line here read as a fifth boundary.
strip <- function(v, col, alpha) if (any(vapply(v, is.null, TRUE))) NULL else
  annotate("rect", xmin = min(v[[1]]$lx, v[[2]]$lx), xmax = max(v[[1]]$lx, v[[2]]$lx),
           ymin = YLIM[1], ymax = YLIM[2], fill = col, alpha = alpha)
vpts <- function(v, fill) if (any(vapply(v, is.null, TRUE))) NULL else
  geom_point(data = bind_rows(v), aes(lx, ly), shape = 21, fill = fill, colour = "grey20",
             size = 1.9, inherit.aes = FALSE)

g <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = RIB, aes(x = lx, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = pf, group = paste(q, par)),
              alpha = 0.16, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(data = LIN, aes(x = lx, y = c1, colour = pf, linetype = qlab, group = paste(q, par)),
            linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_point(data = LIN, aes(x = lx, y = c1, colour = pf), size = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = PCOL, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PCOL, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(QQ$lty, QQ$qlab), name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = 2, keywidth = unit(15, "pt")),
         linetype = guide_legend(order = 2, ncol = 1, keywidth = unit(24, "pt"))) +
  strip(v_open, "grey35", 0.13) + vpts(v_open, "black") +
  strip(v_close, "grey55", 0.10) + vpts(v_close, "white") +
  { if (!any(vapply(v_open, is.null, TRUE)))
      annotate("text", x = mean(c(v_open[[1]]$lx, v_open[[2]]$lx)), y = YLIM[2] - 0.28,
               hjust = 0.5, size = 2.2, lineheight = .95,
               label = paste0("region 3 opens somewhere\nin this strip: N_ch ", rng(v_open))) } +
  { if (!any(vapply(v_close, is.null, TRUE)))
      annotate("text", x = log10(4.3), y = log10(0.042), hjust = 0, size = 2.2, colour = "grey35",
               lineheight = .95, label = paste0("map closes here, EXTRAPOLATED (N_ch ", rng(v_close),
                                                "):\nthis is what the N_ch 2 and 5 runs would pin")) } +
  annotate("text", x = log10(230),  y = log10(0.031), label = "0   Gaussian closure fails",
           size = 2.4, hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey25") +
  annotate("text", x = log10(2200), y = log10(2.5),   label = "1   i + N_ch + honest CI",
           size = 2.8, hjust = 0.5, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = log10(38),   y = log10(3.2),   label = "i but\nnot N_ch", size = 2.1,
           hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey25", lineheight = .95) +
  annotate("text", x = log10(3000), y = log10(6e3),   label = "2   rates + honest CI\n(amplitude needs a prior)",
           size = 2.5, hjust = 0.5, lineheight = .95) +
  annotate("text", x = log10(6000), y = log10(2.4e5), label = "3   ILSE\nis par", size = 2.4,
           hjust = 0.5, lineheight = .95) +
  { if (is.finite(NEVER$nch_min[NEVER$par == "kon"]))
      annotate("text", x = log10(12), y = log10(3e3),
               hjust = 0, size = 2.1, colour = PCOL[["k_on"]], lineheight = .95,
               label = sprintf("k_on unreachable at ANY noise below N_ch %.0f:\nthe line ENDS here, it does not leave the grid",
                               NEVER$nch_min[NEVER$par == "kon"])) } +
  annotate("text", x = log10(90),   y = log10(4e6),   label = "4   nothing estimable",
           size = 2.6, hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey25") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = xbrk, labels = xlab, limits = XLIM, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = ybrk, labels = ylab, limits = YLIM, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = expression(N[ch]), y = "dimensionless instrumental noise") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.title = element_text(size = 8.5),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.justification = "left", legend.box = "vertical",
        legend.box.just = "left", legend.text = element_text(size = 6.9),
        legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), legend.spacing.y = unit(1, "pt"),
        legend.box.margin = margin(-4, 0, 0, -6), legend.key.height = unit(9, "pt"),
        plot.margin = margin(4, 6, 2, 4))
g
# Was Figure_6.pdf until 2026-07-31. The figure is now the `map` chunk at the foot of this notebook;
# this one stays as the version for CHECKING, since the boundaries are here as lines with their
# ribbons and their vertices rather than as the edges of filled regions.
ggsave(arch("Figure_6_lines.pdf"), g, width = 7.0, height = 6.6, device = cairo_pdf)  # cairo: keeps the Delta glyph
ggsave(arch("Figure_6_lines.png"), g, width = 7.0, height = 6.6, dpi = 140)
```

```{r regions, fig.width = 7.6, fig.height = 5.2}
# ---- experimental preparations, from sourced numbers ----------------------------------------------
# Provenance and every figure below: docs/bibliography/recording_configurations/SOURCES.md, with the
# Axon Guide chapter saved beside it. THE CONVERSION IS VERIFIED, from qmodel.h:3740,
#     e = Current_Noise * fs / n_samples   ->  variance per recorded point = Current_Noise / Delta,
# so Current_Noise is a noise POWER SPECTRAL DENSITY and, with label = 1000 * Current_Noise,
#     label = 10 * k_off * sigma_raw^2 / (fs * i^2),
# which at Delta = 0.1 tau = 1 ms and k_off = 100 /s becomes label = (sigma per 1 ms point / i)^2.
# White noise of RMS sigma_B in a bandwidth B gives sigma_Delta^2 = sigma_B^2 / (2 B Delta).
# THE SCALING LEDGER (Luciano, 2026-07-27: which quantities scale linearly and which quadratically).
# Every exponent below is load-bearing, so they are written out rather than left implicit:
#   LINEAR     the macroscopic current in N_ch and in i, separately:  I = N_ch * i * P_open
#   LINEAR     the gating variance in the macroscopic current, and in i as well, because
#              Var_gate = N_ch i^2 p(1-p) = I * i * (1-p)
#   LINEAR     label in the noise power spectral density S, and in k_off at fixed bandwidth
#   QUADRATIC  label in 1/i: the signal is measured in units of i and the rig is not
#   QUADRATIC  S in the rms noise:                        S = sigma^2 / B
#   QUADRATIC  the noise PSD in membrane capacitance for the series-resistance mechanism, because the
#              current noise density is e_n * 2 pi f * C_m, so S grows as C_m^2 (Axon Guide ch. 12)
# The last two together are the reason a bigger preparation loses. N_ch grows LINEARLY with membrane
# area while the instrumental variance grows QUADRATICALLY with it, so r = label/N_ch worsens about
# linearly in area. The excised patch escapes that scaling because its noise is set by the pipette
# dielectric and the headstage rather than by C_m, which is why going from a patch to a whole cell buys
# channels almost for free, and why going from a whole cell to an oocyte does not.
#
# IN OBSERVABLES the same statement is shorter. Substituting N_ch = I/(i P_open),
#     r = label / N_ch = 10 * S * P_open / (tau * i * I)
# so r falls LINEARLY in the macroscopic current and LINEARLY in the unitary current. Once the clamp
# ceiling pins I at I_max, raising expression can only lower i, and r ~ N_ch: every preparation has an
# OPTIMAL channel number N* = I_max / (i_max * P_open), and expressing past it makes things worse.
# Printed below per preparation. The oocyte at 5e7 is an order of magnitude past its own N*.
# THREE PREPARATIONS, AND THE CHANNEL NOW LIVES INSIDE EACH BOX rather than outside all three (scheme
# by Luciano, 2026-07-27). The channel contributes two ranges, shared by every preparation:
#     i   = 1-10 pA, i.e. about 10-170 pS at 60-100 mV of driving force. Covers AMPA at the bottom and
#           glycine or NMDA at the top; it clips CFTR below and BK (25-30 pA at +100 mV) above.
#     tau = 1-30 ms. Covers nAChR, AMPA, P2X2 and glycine; it clips Na_V inactivation (0.3-0.5 ms)
#           below and NMDA or GABA-A deactivation (50-500 ms) above.
# Both extreme corners are real receptors, glycine at high driving force for (10 pA, 30 ms) and AMPA
# for (1 pA, 1 ms), so the rectangle is not empty where it matters.
# tau IS CLIPPED PER PREPARATION, because it is not a free choice: it is the fastest relaxation the
# configuration can resolve. Fast perfusion of an excised patch reaches 0.1 ms, so the whole channel
# range is open to it; whole cell and oocyte are held to about 10 ms by solution exchange and by clamp
# settling, so their window is 10-30 ms. OPEN QUESTION, and it is not cosmetic: for a BATH concentration
# jump the oocyte's exchange is 1-10 s, which would put it outside the 1-30 ms window altogether. The
# 10 ms floor used here is the voltage-step or fast-perfusion case.
#
# TWO CONSTRAINTS CUT CORNERS OFF THE RECTANGLES, both straight out of the ledger above.
#  1. THE CLAMP WINDOW, both ends of it. N_ch and i are independent as biology and coupled as an
#     experiment, because I = N_ch i P_open has to land inside what the configuration can record.
#     THE CEILING is what the clamp can hold: about 2 nA in a patch, 10 nA in whole cell (at
#     Rs = 10 MOhm that is already 100 mV of error), a few tens of uA in TEVC. Because label goes as
#     1/i^2, substituting i = I_max/(N_ch P_open) gives
#         label >= 10 * S * (N_ch P_open)^2 / (tau * I_max^2),
#     so the FLOOR of each box rises as N_ch^2 once the ceiling binds. N* below is where that starts,
#     and it is where each preparation is at its best.
#     THE MINIMUM is the other half of the same statement (Luciano, 2026-07-27): a record has to be
#     big enough to be a record at all, about 0.1 uA in an oocyte, where the endogenous conductances
#     of an uninjected cell are already tens of nA. So FEW CHANNELS HAVE TO BE BIG ONES,
#         i >= I_min / (N_ch P_open),
#     and by the same substitution the CEILING of each box FALLS as N_ch^2 below
#     N_min* = I_min/(i_lo P_open). Two slope-2 diagonals, mirror images, one cutting the bottom right
#     corner and one the top left. Below n_feas = I_min/(i_hi P_open) the configuration is infeasible
#     at any i: even the largest channel available cannot reach I_min. That is a DERIVED left edge for
#     the box, and for the oocyte it lands at 2e4 channels, well below the expression floor used here,
#     so the two statements do not conflict. Both are printed.
#     WHAT THIS COSTS THE ARGUMENT: it removes exactly the corners where the map was least favourable.
#     The patch's worst r falls from 2.5 to 0.63 and the oocyte's from 90 to 22, so the minimum-current
#     cut is not a decoration, it is the difference between crossing two boundaries and one.
#  2. THE SPECTRAL EXPONENT. The y axis is a WHITE noise level, so placing a real rig on it means asking
#     which white level reproduces the variance of a Delta-averaged point. For a rig whose PSD goes as
#     f^p, S_eq = S(B0) * (B/B0)^p with B = 1/Delta = 10/tau, hence
#         label = 10 * S(B0) * (10/(tau B0))^p / (tau i^2),
#     which is 1/tau for white noise, 1/tau^2 at p = 1, 1/tau^3 at p = 2. Taken as p = 1 for the patch
#     (pipette dielectric noise, PSD linear in f) and p = 2 for whole cell and oocyte (series-resistance
#     noise, PSD quadratic in f), both from Axon Guide ch. 12. All three forms AGREE at tau = 10 ms,
#     which is exactly where the sigma values were quoted (B0 = 1 kHz), so the correction pivots on the
#     anchor instead of moving it. It bites at the edges: the patch's fast edge rises 10x and every slow
#     edge drops by 3^p. The white-noise floor is printed alongside so the swing stays visible.
#     LIMITATION: a variance match is not an autocorrelation match. A rising spectrum is high-pass, so a
#     real rig's consecutive Delta-points are slightly anticorrelated where the simulation's are
#     independent. Nothing here claims more than the variance.
#
# NOISE, sigma at B0 = 1 kHz, all from SOURCES.md:
#   patch       0.1-0.5 pA. Brackets the one hard measurement in that file (S = 1.04e-4 pA^2/Hz gives
#               sqrt(1.04e-4 * 1000) = 0.32 pA at 1 kHz), and the true floor may be 2-3x lower.
#   whole cell  1 pA, the author's value; the measured spread in SOURCES.md is 0.4-3 pA at 1 kHz.
#   oocyte      0.5-3 nA. The two ends are the two oocyte methods: 0.5 nA at 1 kHz is S = 250 pA^2/Hz,
#               which is the cut-open figure (1 nA at 3-5 kHz), and 3 nA is conventional TEVC measured
#               off a published trace (Nagel 2025 Nat Commun 16:10367 Fig 8b, S = 1.09e4 pA^2/Hz).
# EXPRESSION LEVELS as set in the table below: patch 10-300, whole cell 20-1e4, oocyte 1e5-5e7 channels
# (Luciano, 2026-07-27). The literature sweep behind them is now written up in
# docs/bibliography/recording_configurations/EXPRESSION_LEVELS.md (23 agents, 159 claims, 134 confirmed).
# THREE OF THESE EDGES HAVE A SOURCED ALTERNATIVE and none is applied here, because they are decisions:
#   patch Imin 10 -> 5 pA        Khanra 2026 Nat Commun 17:3789, a stated Methods acceptance criterion.
#                                Costs the argument: the upper-left diagonal disappears, i returns to
#                                1 pA at the left edge and the patch's worst r rises from 0.63 to 2.5.
#   whole cell Imin 100 -> 500 pA  Li 2017 PLoS ONE, measured over 42,272 wells. Helps: forces i = 3.3 pA
#                                at n_lo and drops that corner about 11x.
#   oocyte n_lo 1e5 -> 8e5       Fujiwara & Kubo 2004 J Physiol 558:31. The 1e5 has no source and is
#                                unreachable at i = 1 pA anyway (50 nA, under the oocyte's own Imin).
# THE PROJECT'S OWN P2X2 STUDY, precisely: it supplies no number on the COUNT axis. On the NOISE axis the
# patch row's 0.1-0.5 pA was originally chosen to bracket that record's S = 1.04e-4 pA^2/Hz, so the
# exclusion was incomplete. That is now closed independently: six laboratories with the seal attached and
# the bandwidth stated give 0.05-0.35 pA at 1 kHz (Smith/Wang/Howe 2000, Prieto & Wollmuth 2010, Rycroft
# & Gibb 2002, Ding & Sachs 1999, Premkumar & Auerbach 1997, McGee 2025; EXPRESSION_LEVELS.md section 2g),
# a band that contains the 0.1-0.5 used here. The patch row no longer rests on the excluded record.
# THE NOISE AXIS IS REFERRED TO k_off, NOT TO THE SAMPLING INTERVAL (Luciano, 2026-07-27, correcting a
# derivation of mine that went round in circles). The definition, and the only thing here that is not
# open, is
#     label = 10 * Current_Noise * k_off / i^2
# with Current_Noise the noise power spectral density S. There is NO Delta in it. Writing instead
# sigma_Delta^2 = S/Delta and substituting Delta = 0.1 tau gives label = (sigma_Delta/i)^2, which is
# algebraically the same thing but only because 10*k_off = 1/Delta at that convention, AND it needs the
# noise to be white to write sigma_Delta^2 = S/Delta at all. The k_off form needs no such assumption, so
# it is the one used here. With S = sigma_B^2/B evaluated at B = k_off = 1/tau,
#     label = 10 * (sigma_{1/tau} / i)^2
# so tau = 1 ms means a 1 kHz band, not 10 kHz.
# CONSEQUENCE WORTH MORE THAN THE CORRECTION: the y axis does not depend on Delta at all. The sampling
# interval moves the BOUNDARIES, which is what DRNG already sweeps, and it does not move a preparation's
# vertical position. The two axes are independent rather than coupled through a convention.
#
# WHAT IS NOT KNOWN, stated plainly so it is not re-derived a fourth time. label needs S at that row's
# own k_off. That is the rig's noise SPECTRUM, and it is not measured for any of the three preparations:
# each has ONE rms figure at ONE band. How many decades of label a decade of tau buys is therefore NOT
# DERIVABLE from anything in this file. Three attempts at it by assuming a spectrum shape gave 9.9, 4.05
# and 1.39 decades, all arithmetic on an invented spectrum and none of them evidence. Until two measured
# sigma values per preparation exist, tau contributes NOTHING to the height of a box here, and the boxes
# below are drawn from the i range and the rig-to-rig spread alone. The gap is left visible on purpose.
# HOW TO MEASURE IT, when it is done: TRACE_WIDTH_METHOD.md, on a segment with NO channel activity. At
# long tau the gating noise takes over, and this file's own excised-patch record has 99 % of the variance
# of a 13.7 ms point coming from unliganded gating, a factor 93 over the instrument. Measured carelessly,
# "the noise at the tau of the kinetics" returns the quantity being estimated.
# ONE MORE MISSPECIFICATION, unrelated to the closure: the simulation adds Gaussian WHITE noise. A real
# series-resistance-limited rig is Gaussian and coloured, hence high-pass, so its consecutive samples are
# anticorrelated where the simulation's are independent. Matching S at one band does not match that, and
# nothing here models it.
B0    <- 1000     # Hz, retained only to convert the sigma values that were quoted at 1 kHz
I_LO  <- 1        # pA, smallest unitary current considered
I_HI  <- 10       # pA, largest
POPEN <- 0.5      # the model's open probability at saturation
lbl <- function(S, tau, i) 10 * S / (tau * i^2)   # = 10 * S_tilde, the sweep's own label. See note above
psd <- function(sig, B) sig^2 / B                 # rms in a bandwidth B -> power spectral density
# Imin for the patch (10 pA) and whole cell (100 pA) are placeholders of the same kind as the oocyte's
# 0.1 uA and have NOT been signed off; the oocyte value is the author's. Whole cell's N_min* = 200 falls
# below its own n_lo, so that row is unaffected either way.
# sig_lo and sig_hi are the RIG-TO-RIG spread at the band named in sig_band, which is a different thing
# from the band-to-band change of sigma across each row's own tau range. Only the first is known, so tau
# contributes NOTHING to the height of a box here. That is the honest current state and it is deliberate:
# the missing measurement shows up as a box that is too short rather than as an invented number.
# WHOLE CELL, tau = 0.5-1000 ms and N_ch = 20-1e4, settled with Luciano 2026-07-27. The N_ch edges are
# DERIVED, not assumed: 20 = 100 pA/(10 pA x 0.5) and 1e4 = 5 nA/(1 pA x 0.5), so they encode Imin and
# Imax rather than an expression guess. Imax = 5 nA is his (at Rs compensated to 2 MOhm that is already
# 20 mV of error); Imin = 100 pA is still a placeholder. STILL OPEN on this row: the i floor, since Cav
# with physiological Ca carries 0.3-0.5 pA and label goes as 1/i^2, so dropping I_LO to 0.3 would raise
# every box top 11x; and whether the row is HEK or native, since a 70-150 pF neuron or myocyte is 3-10x
# noisier than the 20-30 pF HEK cell the 1 pA came from, and the fast half of that literature is native.
PREP <- tribble(~name,           ~n_lo, ~n_hi, ~sig_lo, ~sig_hi, ~sig_band, ~tau_lo, ~tau_hi, ~Imin, ~Imax,
  "excised outside-out patch",      10,   300,     0.1,     0.5,      1000,    1e-3,    3e-2,   1e1,   2e3,
  "whole cell",                     20,   1e4,     1.0,     1.0,      1000,    5e-4,       1,   1e2,   5e3,
  "oocyte, two-electrode",         1e5,   5e7,     5e2,     3e3,      1000,    1e-2,    3e-2,   1e5,   3e7) %>%
  mutate(xlo = log10(n_lo), xhi = log10(n_hi),
         S_lo = psd(sig_lo, sig_band), S_hi = psd(sig_hi, sig_band),
         nstar = pmin(pmax(Imax / (I_HI * POPEN), n_lo), n_hi),   # ceiling starts to bind: floor turns up
         nmin_star = pmin(pmax(Imin / (I_LO * POPEN), n_lo), n_hi), # minimum binds: ceiling turns down
         nfeas = Imin / (I_HI * POPEN),                           # derived left edge: below it, no i works
         yhi = log10(lbl(S_hi, tau_lo, pmax(I_LO, Imin / (n_hi * POPEN)))),   # top at the right edge
         yhi_l = log10(lbl(S_hi, tau_lo, pmax(I_LO, Imin / (n_lo * POPEN)))), # top at the left edge
         ylo = log10(lbl(S_lo, tau_hi, I_HI)),                                # flat part of the floor
         ylo_r = log10(lbl(S_lo, tau_hi, pmin(I_HI, Imax / (n_hi * POPEN)))))
# The footprint, both diagonals: the top follows i >= Imin/(N P_open) and the floor i <= Imax/(N P_open).
# Where the two meet the box PINCHES to zero height: there is no freedom left in i, so nothing to draw.
POLY <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(PREP)), function(k) {
  p  <- PREP[k, ]
  xs <- sort(unique(c(seq(p$xlo, p$xhi, length.out = 120), log10(p$nstar), log10(p$nmin_star))))
  xs <- xs[xs >= p$xlo & xs <= p$xhi]
  N  <- 10^xs
  itop <- pmax(I_LO, p$Imin / (N * POPEN))   # few channels have to be big ones
  ibot <- pmin(I_HI, p$Imax / (N * POPEN))   # many channels have to be small ones
  tibble(name = p$name, x = c(xs, rev(xs)),
         y = c(log10(lbl(p$S_hi, p$tau_lo, itop)), rev(log10(lbl(p$S_lo, p$tau_hi, ibot)))))
}))
# r over the whole footprint, not just its corners: the extrema sit where the diagonals start to bind.
RR <- POLY %>% mutate(r = y - x) %>% group_by(name) %>% summarise(r_lo = min(r), r_hi = max(r))
cat("\nfigure_7: three preparations, in the sweep's own label = 10 * S * k_off / i^2 = 10 * S_tilde\n")
print(as.data.frame(PREP %>% left_join(RR, by = "name") %>% transmute(name,
      N_ch    = sprintf("%.3g - %.3g", n_lo, n_hi),
      tau_ms  = sprintf("%.3g - %.3g", tau_lo * 1e3, tau_hi * 1e3),
      sigma_pA_at = sprintf("%.3g - %.3g @ %.0f Hz", sig_lo, sig_hi, sig_band),
      label   = sprintf("%.3g - %.3g", 10^pmin(ylo, ylo_r), 10^pmax(yhi, yhi_l)),
      S_tilde = sprintf("%.3g - %.3g", 10^pmin(ylo, ylo_r)/10, 10^pmax(yhi, yhi_l)/10),
      r       = sprintf("%.2g - %.2g", 10^r_lo, 10^r_hi),
      N_opt   = sprintf("%.3g", nstar),
      N_feasible_above = sprintf("%.3g", nfeas))), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- the one real experiment: WITHDRAWN 2026-07-27 --------------------------------------------------
# The box drawn here used to be Moffatt & Hume 2007's own P2X2 outside-out record, measured from
# projects/p2x2/data/experiments/, at N_ch = 1777-2961 with an arrow for a x93 unliganded-gating floor.
# It is withdrawn on the author's instruction, for two reasons that both bear on the numbers: the
# records SUM three traces per response, so the 1777 pA peak is not one patch's current (it would be
# about 590 pA, and N_ch about 590-990, with sigma smaller by sqrt(3) so that S falls 3x too, which
# moves the box diagonally without changing r), and the preparation shows unliganded gating, so its
# x93 noise floor is a property of that preparation and not a generic feature of an excised patch.
# The excised-patch box above is therefore carried entirely by other laboratories.
# TO RESTORE: set SHOW_EXP to TRUE and rebuild EXP here. Left as a switch rather than deleted, because
# whether the figure keeps one worked example is still open.
SHOW_EXP <- FALSE

# THE SIMPLIFIED SIBLING — the version for reading; the boundary figure above is the version for
# checking. Same measurements, read as areas. Four rules it follows, each fixing something the first
# draft got wrong:
#  1. ORDERED fill, not categorical. The regions are a ladder (the likelihood buys two things, then
#     one, then none, then the experiment is empty), so the ramp goes dark -> pale in that order and
#     the reader sees the ordering without reading a word. Region 0 is a DIFFERENT kind of failure
#     (the model, not the experiment), so it gets its own hue rather than a rung of the ramp.
#  2. Labels say WHAT TO DO, not what the diagnostic did. This is a usage map. The four boundary
#     labels are deliberately PARALLEL, because they are the 2x2 written out: two of them say
#     "<method> becomes honest" (the likelihood at the bottom, least squares higher up) and two say
#     "<parameter> no longer measurable" (the amplitude pair, then k_off). Phrasing one of them
#     differently -- "the closure fails", "i and N_ch stop separating" -- hid that structure.
#  3. MEASURED vs EXTRAPOLATED is visible: heavy line inside the simulated N_ch span, faint dotted
#     outside, dots on the actual crossings. The first draft drew fitted power laws to the plot edges
#     and so claimed confidence it does not have — the floor, in particular, is measured only over
#     N_ch 10-100.
#  4. Everything clamped to the panel, so no ribbon can vanish against the axis limit.
fitb <- function(qq, pp) {
  d <- CR %>% filter(q == qq, par == pp, D == DREF, is.finite(c1))
  if (nrow(d) < 2) return(NULL)
  list(co = coef(lm(c1 ~ lx, d)), lo = min(d$lx), hi = max(d$lx), pts = d)
}
FB <- list(floor = fitb("floor", "koff"), ilost = fitb("se", "i"),
           hon = fitb("lse", "koff"),     dead = fitb("se", "koff"))
ev  <- function(f, x) f$co[1] + f$co[2] * x
cl  <- function(y) pmin(pmax(y, YLIM[1]), YLIM[2])
gx  <- seq(XLIM[1], XLIM[2], length.out = 500)

# the preparation footprints, clipped to the panel. N* is marked only where it is VISIBLE: for whole
# cell the whole floor sits below the panel, so its upturn cannot be shown and marking it would put a
# dot on the axis that means nothing.
POLYC <- POLY %>% mutate(y = cl(y))
NSTAR <- PREP %>% filter(n_hi > nstar * 1.001, ylo > YLIM[1]) %>%
  transmute(name, x = log10(nstar), y = ylo)
OFFB  <- PREP %>% filter(ylo < YLIM[1])
cat("\nfigure_7: preparation footprints, clipped to the panel\n")
print(as.data.frame(PREP %>% transmute(name,
      floor_true = sprintf("%.3g", 10^ylo), floor_at_right_edge = sprintf("%.3g", 10^ylo_r),
      top = sprintf("%.3g", 10^yhi),
      off_panel_bottom = ifelse(ylo < YLIM[1], "yes", "no"))), row.names = FALSE)

# the floor is measured to be ABSENT above N_ch 200 (IR is calibrated at every noise there), which is
# a measurement and not an extrapolation: pin it to the panel floor rather than extending the fit.
y_floor <- ifelse(gx > log10(150), log10(NOISE_MIN), cl(ev(FB$floor, gx)))
y_i     <- cl(ev(FB$ilost, gx)); y_hon <- cl(ev(FB$hon, gx)); y_dead <- cl(ev(FB$dead, gx))
R <- tibble(x = gx,
  r0_lo = YLIM[1],                r0_hi = pmax(YLIM[1], pmin(y_floor, y_i)),
  r1_lo = pmin(y_floor, y_i),     r1_hi = pmax(pmin(y_floor, y_i), y_i),
  r2_lo = y_i,                    r2_hi = pmax(y_i, pmin(y_hon, y_dead)),
  r3_lo = pmin(y_hon, y_dead),    r3_hi = pmax(pmin(y_hon, y_dead), y_dead),
  r4_lo = y_dead,                 r4_hi = YLIM[2]) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("r"), cl))

# 0 = its own hue; 1..4 = one ramp. Regions 1 and 2 lightened 2026-07-31: #3E9B62 was dark enough
# that the grey15 measured points and boundary lines drawn on top of it stopped reading.
RC   <- c("#B9A7D0", "#8FCBA6", "#C8E6D2", "#FBE08A", "#EFEFEF")
RLAB <- c("0  the likelihood itself fails",
          "1  amplitude and rates, with an honest interval",
          "2  rates only, with an honest interval",
          "3  least squares is at par",
          "4  nothing measurable")
# One mapped layer instead of five hardcoded fills, so the regions get a key. The in-panel prose
# says what to do; the key says which numbered region the text and the caption are talking about.
RLONG <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(0:4, function(k) tibble::tibble(
  x   = R$x,
  lo  = R[[paste0("r", k, "_lo")]],
  hi  = R[[paste0("r", k, "_hi")]],
  reg = factor(RLAB[k + 1], levels = RLAB))))
MEAS <- range(c(FB$ilost$pts$lx, FB$hon$pts$lx, FB$dead$pts$lx, FB$floor$pts$lx))

lineseg <- function(f, cap = NULL) {                      # heavy where measured, faint outside
  hi <- if (is.null(cap)) f$hi else min(f$hi, cap)
  xin <- seq(f$lo, hi, length.out = 120)
  xout <- gx[(gx < f$lo & gx > f$lo - 0.5) | (gx > hi & gx < hi + 0.5)]
  list(geom_line(data = tibble(x = xout, y = cl(ev(f, xout))), aes(x, y),
                 linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "12", colour = "grey30"),
       geom_line(data = tibble(x = xin, y = cl(ev(f, xin))), aes(x, y),
                 linewidth = 0.7, colour = "grey15"),
       geom_point(data = f$pts %>% mutate(y = cl(c1)), aes(lx, y), size = 1.1, colour = "grey15"))
}
lab <- function(x, y, t, sz = 3.0, fc = "plain", col = "grey10", hj = 0.5)
  annotate("text", x = log10(x), y = log10(y), label = t, size = sz, fontface = fc,
           colour = col, hjust = hj, lineheight = 1.0)
# boundary labels set ALONG each line. The angle is the fitted slope carried into device space:
# x spans diff(XLIM) decades over ~6.3 in and y spans diff(YLIM) over ~4.3 in. Approximate on
# purpose -- this is a concept map, and these labels are what make it readable without the caption.
ASPECT <- (diff(XLIM) / diff(YLIM)) * (4.1 / 6.4)   # panel is ~6.3 x 4.1 in once the caption left
blab <- function(x, f, t, dy = 0.3, sz = 2.35) {
  lx <- log10(x)
  annotate("text", x = lx, y = ev(f, lx) + dy, label = t, size = sz, colour = "grey15",
           angle = atan(f$co[2] * ASPECT) * 180 / pi, hjust = 0.5)
}

gr <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = RLONG, aes(x = x, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = reg), alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = stats::setNames(RC, RLAB), name = NULL,
                    # the region-4 fill is near-white, so the key needs an outline to exist against the page
                    guide = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE, order = 1,
                                         override.aes = list(colour = "grey55", linewidth = .2))) +
  lineseg(FB$floor, cap = log10(150)) + lineseg(FB$ilost) +
  lineseg(FB$hon) + lineseg(FB$dead) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = XLIM[1], xmax = XLIM[2], ymin = YLIM[1], ymax = log10(NOISE_MIN),
           fill = "white", alpha = 0.72) +

  annotate("text", x = XLIM[2] - 0.05, y = log10(0.0155), hjust = 1, size = 2.2, colour = "grey40",
           label = "no data below here: 0.05 is the lowest noise simulated") +
  annotate("segment", x = MEAS, xend = MEAS, y = YLIM[1], yend = YLIM[2],
           colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "22") +
  annotate("text", x = mean(MEAS), y = YLIM[2] - 0.22, label = "simulated range of N_ch",
           size = 2.2, colour = "grey35") +
  blab(30,   FB$floor, "the likelihood becomes honest",  0.45) +
  blab(600,  FB$ilost, "i and N_ch no longer measurable", 0.32) +
  blab(1600, FB$hon,   "least squares becomes honest",  0.34) +
  blab(55,   FB$dead,  "k_off no longer measurable",    0.36) +
  geom_polygon(data = POLYC, aes(x, y, group = name),
               fill = "white", alpha = 0.35, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_polygon(data = POLYC, aes(x, y, group = name),
               fill = NA, colour = "grey10", linewidth = 0.45, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = PREP %>% mutate(ly = pmin(yhi, YLIM[2] - 0.15) + 0.30,

                                   hj = c(0.5, 1, 0.5)),
            aes(x = lx, y = ly, label = name, hjust = hj),
            size = 2.3, fontface = "bold", colour = "grey5", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  # N*: past it the clamp ceiling forces i down and the floor turns upward as N_ch^2
  { if (nrow(NSTAR)) geom_point(data = NSTAR, aes(x, y), shape = 21, fill = "white",
                                colour = "grey10", size = 1.5, inherit.aes = FALSE) } +
  { if (nrow(NSTAR)) geom_text(data = NSTAR %>% slice(1), aes(x, y),
      label = "N*: past here the clamp ceiling\nforces i down and the floor\nturns upward as N_ch^2",
      hjust = 1, nudge_x = -0.12, nudge_y = -0.40, size = 2.05, colour = "grey20",
      lineheight = .95, inherit.aes = FALSE) } +
  # boxes whose floor leaves the panel: quieter than anything the sweep simulated
  { if (nrow(OFFB)) geom_segment(data = OFFB, aes(x = (xlo + xhi) / 2, xend = (xlo + xhi) / 2,

  { if (nrow(OFFB)) annotate("text", x = log10(3.2), y = YLIM[1] + 0.62, hjust = 0, size = 2.05,
```
