```{r frontiers, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5.6}
# THE FRONTIER VERSION (Luciano, 2026-07-26). The criterion is the author's convention and the reader
# cannot resolve it, so instead of picking one and drawing a line, BOTH criteria are drawn and the
# strip between them is left blank: a transition zone where the answer depends on how strict you are.
# What survives as solid colour is what holds under BOTH criteria. The weakness of the sharp-line
# version (the region-3 vertex moves from N_ch 120 to 1368 with the criterion) becomes the content:
# region 3 simply has no core until the two bands separate.
#
# ONE thing is deliberately NOT banded: the sampling interval. Delta is a design choice the READER
# makes and knows, so it stays fixed at the reference and is stated. Banding it too would widen every
# frontier by another 0.6-1 decade and swallow regions 2 and 3 entirely -- which is itself a measured
# fact, and is why the interval gets its own treatment in the companion figure instead.
#
# REGION 4 IS DEFINED BY k_off, THE LAST PARAMETER STANDING, and that is not a convenience. Defining
# it as "not every rate is measurable" (i.e. by k_on) makes the whole plane below N_ch ~52 read
# "nothing useful left", which is plainly false: at 10 channels you still get k_off, the conductance
# and the channel count. Losing k_on is its own rung, not the end of the ladder, so it is drawn as an
# internal boundary with its own label, and the fact that k_on is out of reach at ANY noise below
# N_ch ~52 is marked on the axis rather than swallowing four regions.
fit2 <- function(qq, pp) {
  d <- CR %>% filter(q == qq, par == pp, D == DREF)
  f1 <- d %>% filter(is.finite(c1)); f2 <- d %>% filter(is.finite(c2))
  if (nrow(f1) < 2) return(NULL)
  list(a = coef(lm(c1 ~ lx, f1)),
       b = if (nrow(f2) >= 2) coef(lm(c2 ~ lx, f2)) else coef(lm(c1 ~ lx, f1)),
       pts = f1)
}
FF <- list(floor = fit2("floor", "koff"), ilost = fit2("se", "i"),
           hon = fit2("lse", "koff"),     dead = fit2("se", "koff"),
           kon = fit2("se", "kon"))
gx <- seq(XLIM[1], XLIM[2], length.out = 500)
bnd <- function(f) { y1 <- f$a[1] + f$a[2] * gx; y2 <- f$b[1] + f$b[2] * gx
                     list(lo = cl(pmin(y1, y2)), hi = cl(pmax(y1, y2))) }
Bf <- bnd(FF$floor); Bi <- bnd(FF$ilost); Bh <- bnd(FF$hon); Bd <- bnd(FF$dead)
Bk <- bnd(FF$kon)
off <- gx > log10(150)                       # closure measured ABSENT above N_ch ~150
Bf$lo[off] <- log10(NOISE_MIN); Bf$hi[off] <- log10(NOISE_MIN)
# NOTE, and it cost a wrong claim (caught by Luciano, 2026-07-26): NEVER$nch_min is computed at the
# REFERENCE interval only, so "k_on is unreachable below N_ch 52" was an artefact of fixing Delta.
# Minimising over Delta as well, IR reaches SE(k_on) = 0.267 at N_ch 10 with Delta.k_off = 0.01
# (0.375 at 0.1, 0.511 at 1). ILSE does NOT: its best is 0.708 at every Delta and every noise. So at
# few channels the rate boundary is genuinely method-dependent, a factor 2.7, and must not be sourced
# from ILSE there. No "unreachable" marker is drawn.

FR <- tibble(x = gx,
  r0_lo = YLIM[1],  r0_hi = Bf$lo,
  r1_lo = Bf$hi,    r1_hi = pmax(Bf$hi, Bi$lo),
  r2_lo = Bi$hi,    r2_hi = pmax(Bi$hi, pmin(Bh$lo, Bd$lo)),
  r3_lo = Bh$hi,    r3_hi = pmax(Bh$hi, Bd$lo),
  r4_lo = Bd$hi,    r4_hi = YLIM[2]) %>% mutate(across(starts_with("r"), cl))
CORE <- c("#B9A7D0", "#3E9B62", "#9ED4A8", "#F9D77A", "#D6D6D6")
fillc <- function(k) geom_ribbon(data = FR, aes(x = x, ymin = .data[[paste0("r", k, "_lo")]],
                                                ymax = .data[[paste0("r", k, "_hi")]]),
                                 fill = CORE[k + 1], alpha = 0.95)
edgeb <- function(B) list(
  geom_line(data = tibble(x = gx, y = B$lo), aes(x, y), linewidth = .26, linetype = "22", colour = "grey35"),
  geom_line(data = tibble(x = gx, y = B$hi), aes(x, y), linewidth = .26, linetype = "22", colour = "grey35"))

gf <- ggplot() +
  lapply(0:4, fillc) + edgeb(Bf) + edgeb(Bi) + edgeb(Bh) + edgeb(Bd) +
  # k_on is NOT drawn here, and that is a scope decision, not an omission. Its boundary CROSSES the
  # others: at N_ch 1e3 the amplitude pair is lost first (noise ~3e2) and k_on much later (~1.4e4),
  # but at N_ch 10 the order flips. So k_on is not a rung of this ladder. It is not a method choice
  # either -- IR and ILSE lose it within a few percent of each other except at few channels -- it is a
  # property of the PROTOCOL: one concentration jump determines k_on only through the difference
  # between the pulse rate and the washout rate. If you need k_on, the fix is a second concentration,
  # not a better likelihood. That belongs in the text, not on a usage map.
  lapply(list(FF$floor, FF$ilost, FF$hon, FF$dead), function(f)
    geom_point(data = f$pts %>% mutate(y = cl(c1)), aes(lx, y), size = 1.0, colour = "grey20")) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = XLIM[1], xmax = XLIM[2], ymin = YLIM[1], ymax = log10(NOISE_MIN),
           fill = "white", alpha = 0.75) +
  annotate("segment", x = XLIM[1], xend = XLIM[2], y = log10(NOISE_MIN), yend = log10(NOISE_MIN),
           colour = "grey45", linewidth = .3, linetype = "22") +
  annotate("text", x = XLIM[2] - 0.05, y = log10(0.0125), hjust = 1, size = 2.1, colour = "grey40",
           label = "no data below here: 0.05 is the lowest noise simulated") +
  annotate("segment", x = MEAS, xend = MEAS, y = YLIM[1], yend = YLIM[2],
           colour = "grey40", linewidth = .3, linetype = "22") +
  annotate("text", x = mean(MEAS), y = YLIM[2] - 0.20, label = "simulated range of N_ch",
           size = 2.1, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_polygon(data = POLYC, aes(x, y, group = name),
               fill = "white", alpha = 0.35, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_polygon(data = POLYC, aes(x, y, group = name),
               fill = NA, colour = "grey10", linewidth = 0.45, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = PREP %>% mutate(ly = pmin(yhi, YLIM[2] - 0.15) + 0.30,
                                   lx = c((xlo[1]+xhi[1])/2, xlo[2] - 0.10, (xlo[3]+xhi[3])/2),
                                   hj = c(0.5, 1, 0.5)),
            aes(x = lx, y = ly, label = name, hjust = hj),
            size = 2.3, fontface = "bold", colour = "grey5", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  lab(3000, 1.6, "USE THE LIKELIHOOD\nconductance, channel count, and\nan error bar you can trust", 2.9, "bold") +
  lab(5000, 1.6e4, "USE THE LIKELIHOOD,\nWITH A PRIOR on the amplitude", 2.5) +
  lab(13000, 2e6, "LEAST SQUARES\nIS ENOUGH", 2.5, "bold", hj = 1) +
  lab(55, 3e6, "REDESIGN THE EXPERIMENT", 2.6) +
  lab(17, 0.105, "THE LIKELIHOOD FAILS", 2.2, "bold") +
  lab(24, 2.2e4, "blank strips are the transitions:\nthere the answer depends on\nhow strict a criterion you use",
      2.15, "italic", "grey25", 0) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = xbrk, labels = xlab, limits = XLIM, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = ybrk, labels = ylab, limits = YLIM, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = expression(N[ch]), y = "dimensionless instrumental noise") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "white", linewidth = .18),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.title = element_text(size = 8.5),
        plot.margin = margin(4, 6, 2, 4))
gf
ggsave(arch("Figure_6_frontiers.pdf"), gf, width = 7.0, height = 5.6, device = cairo_pdf)
ggsave(arch("Figure_6_frontiers.png"), gf, width = 7.0, height = 5.6, dpi = 140)
```

## The figure

THE MAP. Same plane, same cells, read as areas. Every cell is filled with WHICH parameters survive,
not with how many: the count conflates the two cases the figure exists to separate. Over the 80
cells at the reference interval the surviving subsets are

    all four   {k_on, k_off, i, N_ch}   51        two   {k_off, i}      11   <- amplitude present
    three      {k_off, i, N_ch}          1        two   {k_on, k_off}    5   <- amplitude gone
    one        {k_off}                   6        none  {}               6

and the two rows labelled "two" are opposite answers to the only question that decides which tool is
needed. LEAST SQUARES HOLDS THE UNITARY CURRENT FIXED AND CANNOT SEPARATE THE CHANNEL COUNT FROM IT,
so where the amplitude is recoverable it is not a candidate at all, and not because its interval is
wrong: it does not estimate those parameters. Where it IS a candidate, the rates, the only question
left is whose interval is calibrated. Five regions:

    violet      the likelihood's own interval is not calibrated, whatever the yield; it overrides
    green       i and k_off at least, usually all four: only the likelihood can deliver this
    pale green  the rates only, and least squares still reports an interval that is too narrow
    amber       the rates only, and least squares is calibrated too
    near-white  nothing measurable

COUNTING WAS ADOPTED (revisions AF to AL) BECAUSE THE BOUNDARIES ARE NOT NESTED: slopes run +1.1 to
+2.2, so they cross and a ladder of count levels inverts. At THIS resolution they are nested, with no
counterexample in the 80 cells: amplitude implies rates, N_ch never survives without i, no subset
carries k_on without k_off. So the partition needs exactly two measurability boundaries, i and
k_off, and k_on and N_ch stay as thin interior lines that subdivide the green region without
partitioning it.

DOES THE DRAWING AGREE WITH THE CELLS? Every earlier revision drew fitted lines over measured cells
and never asked. Classified twice, once from each cell's own measurements and once from the four
fitted lines, 78 of the 80 agree. Both failures are outside a fit's own support: N_ch 5 for the i
boundary, which is fitted from 10, and N_ch 200 for the calibration boundary, which is fitted to 100.
The chunk prints the confusion table on every render.

WHAT IS MEASURED AND WHAT IS NOT. The cells stop at N_ch 1e4 and the panel runs to 1.2e8, so 56% of
the width is fitted power law carried past its own support, the whole oocyte box included. Three
marks say so, none of them a colour: the fills are veiled with sparse white stripes past the last
simulated column, each boundary is solid only over the N_ch span where its own crossings were found
and dashed outside it, and the crossings are drawn as open dots. Per-boundary support: i 10-1e4,
k_off 10-1e3, k_on 5-1e4, N_ch 5-1e4, IR calibration 5-100, ILSE calibration 10-1e4. The last is
fitted over a decade and drawn over seven, which is why it thins where it is extended.

THREE CLASSES OF MARK, three ways of setting them, so that no two kinds of statement look alike:

    dark on plain white       a PARAMETER      i, k_off, k_on, N_ch     names a thin black line
    white barred in dark      an ALGORITHM     ILSE, IR                  names a white cased line
    white on solid            a PREPARATION    the three footprints     names a real experiment
    italic grey on white      an editorial note                         the key's own asides

CALIBRATED, NOT "HONEST", as of 2026-07-31. The property is that the reported Fisher covariance
equals the actual sampling covariance, which is what calibration names and what the rest of the
manuscript already calls it. "Honest" is also taken: an honest confidence interval is one whose
coverage holds uniformly over a class of parameters, a stronger and different property.

<!-- DEPENDS ON THE `regions` CHUNK, which is where PREP, POLY and POLYC are built. If that chunk is
     ever retired, the preparation table has to move up into `geometry` first.
     NUDGE moves two footprint EDGES off the simulated columns for legibility and is OFF: whole
     cell's 20 and 1e4 are DERIVED from Imin and Imax, so the drawn box would stop stating them. The
     collision it was for is solved instead by the white ring on the cells, which costs no number.
     HATCH_BAD writes the sibling in which the region where the likelihood's interval is not
     calibrated is hatched OVER the yield colour instead of replaced, so that corner keeps saying
     that the amplitude is recoverable there and only the interval is wrong. The purple override is
     the figure, decided 2026-07-31; the sibling is kept because the choice is still live.
     CHOICE CLOSED 2026-08-26: the manuscript's Figure 7 float now includes Figure_7_hatch, so THE
     SIBLING IS THE BODY FIGURE and the purple one is the alternative. Both are still written on
     every knit and nothing here changes. Why: the key's own row already says "use MacroIR, but not
     its reported interval", which is the hatch's claim and not the purple one's; Figure 6 resolves
     that same corner at about a factor of 1.5, correctable, while the purple fill erases what is
     recoverable there; and the corner is where the recursion buys the most precision on the rates
     (median ratio 1.64), so a fill that reads as "nothing to see here" is backwards. The two
     textures do not collide: the veil is white, wide and on the right-hand columns, the hatch is
     black, tight and in the left-hand corner, and no cell carries both. Reverting is one token in
     the manuscript's includegraphics plus "violet" in the caption. -->

```{r map, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5.9}
PT <- function(pt) pt * 0.3527
TH <- log10(2)

ir   <- IR %>% distinct(what, par, nch, noise, D, .keep_all = TRUE)
irse <- ir %>% filter(what == "var")  %>% transmute(par, nch, noise, D, se = sqrt(pmax(v, 0)))
irdi <- ir %>% filter(what == "dist") %>% transmute(par, nch, noise, D, d  = abs(log(v)))
lsed <- ILSE %>% filter(what == "dist", par == "koff") %>% distinct(nch, noise, D, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
        transmute(nch, noise, D, l = abs(log(v)))

CELL <- irse %>% filter(D == DREF) %>% group_by(nch, noise) %>%
  summarise(A = sum(se < TH), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(irdi %>% filter(D == DREF) %>% inner_join(irse %>% filter(D == DREF),
              by = c("par","nch","noise")) %>% group_by(nch, noise) %>%
              summarise(irbad = if (!any(se < TH)) 0 else as.numeric(!all(d[se < TH] < log(1.15))),
                        .groups = "drop"), by = c("nch","noise")) %>%
  left_join(lsed %>% filter(D == DREF) %>% select(nch, noise, l), by = c("nch","noise"))

# a boundary = the noise at which a quantity crosses a level, per N_ch, then a log-log fit.
# lo/hi are the N_ch span over which crossings were actually FOUND; from here on that is carried
# through to the drawing instead of being discarded.
fitline <- function(d, col, lev, rising) {
  cr <- d %>% group_by(nch) %>%
    summarise(c = cross1(log10(noise), .data[[col]], lev, rising), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(is.finite(c)) %>% mutate(lx = log10(nch))
  if (nrow(cr) < 2) return(NULL)
  list(co = coef(lm(c ~ lx, cr)), lo = min(cr$lx), hi = max(cr$lx), pts = cr)
}
# ONE BOUNDARY PER PARAMETER, not one per count level: the boundaries are not nested (slopes +1.1 to
# +2.2), so they cross, and counting how many lie above a point is correct whatever they do.
PB <- lapply(c("i","koff","kon","Nch"), function(p)
  fitline(irse %>% filter(D == DREF, par == p) %>% rename(v = se), "v", TH, TRUE))
names(PB) <- c("i","koff","kon","Nch")
BH  <- fitline(CELL %>% filter(!is.na(irbad)), "irbad", 0.5, FALSE)   # below it IR is dishonest
BL  <- fitline(CELL %>% filter(!is.na(l)), "l", log(1.15), FALSE)     # above it least squares is honest
for (n in c("i","koff","kon","Nch")) cat(sprintf("SE(%-4s): slope %+.2f, %d crossings, N_ch %g-%g\n",
  n, PB[[n]]$co[2], nrow(PB[[n]]$pts), 10^PB[[n]]$lo, 10^PB[[n]]$hi))
for (n in c("BH","BL")) cat(sprintf("%-4s     slope %+.2f, %d crossings, N_ch %g-%g\n",
  n, get(n)$co[2], nrow(get(n)$pts), 10^get(n)$lo, 10^get(n)$hi))

XQ   <- c(log10(6), log10(1.2e8))
ev2  <- function(f, x) if (is.null(f)) rep(-Inf, length(x)) else f$co[1] + f$co[2]*x
# The veil does not start ON the last simulated column -- there ARE simulations there, and a rule
# drawn through that column reads as if it were excluded. It starts half a grid step past it, and
# the grid step that matters is NOT the 1-2-5 spacing of the columns: the 1-2-5 columns (20, 50,
# 200, 500, 2000, 5000) all stop at noise 10, so none of them can produce a crossing at the noise
# where these boundaries live. The columns that carry the sweep upward are 10, 100, 1000, 1e4 --
# one per decade, each reaching a decade higher in noise than the last (1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 1e7) -- so
# for every boundary drawn here the step is a DECADE, the column after 1e4 would have been 1e5, and
# the veil begins at 1e4.5 = 3.16e4. Taken from the data rather than written in, so it follows the
# sweep if the sweep is extended.
DEEP  <- (CELL %>% group_by(nch) %>% summarise(hi = max(noise), .groups = "drop") %>%
          filter(hi > 10))$nch
XLAST <- log10(max(CELL$nch))                       # last simulated column
XSTEP <- median(diff(log10(sort(DEEP))))            # spacing of the columns that reach high noise
XSIM  <- XLAST + XSTEP / 2                          # where the veil begins
cat(sprintf("\ncells: N_ch %g-%g, noise label %g-%g; panel N_ch %g-%g -> %.0f%% of the width is extrapolated\n",
  min(CELL$nch), max(CELL$nch), min(CELL$noise), max(CELL$noise), 10^XQ[1], 10^XQ[2],
  100 * (XQ[2] - XLAST) / diff(XQ)))
cat(sprintf("columns reaching past noise 10: %s -> step %.2f decades; veil edge at N_ch %.3g\n",
  paste(sort(DEEP), collapse = ", "), XSTEP, 10^XSIM))

PAL <- c(amp = "#238B45", rate = "#A1D99B", lse = "#FD8D3C",
         none = "#F7F7F7", bad = "#9E9AC8")

# ---- exact regions -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sutherland-Hodgman against a half-plane f <= 0. Every boundary is y = a + b x, so the regions are
# the cells of a line arrangement and can be written down instead of sampled.
clip1 <- function(P, f) {
  if (!nrow(P)) return(P)
  s <- f(P$x, P$y); n <- nrow(P); out <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    j <- if (i == n) 1L else i + 1L
    if (s[i] <= 0) out[[length(out) + 1]] <- P[i, ]
    if (s[i] * s[j] < 0) {
      t <- s[i] / (s[i] - s[j])
      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(x = P$x[i] + t * (P$x[j] - P$x[i]),
                                           y = P$y[i] + t * (P$y[j] - P$y[i]))
    }
  }
  if (!length(out)) P[0, ] else do.call(rbind, out)
}
area <- function(P) { n <- nrow(P); if (n < 3) return(0)
  j <- c(2:n, 1); abs(sum(P$x * P$y[j] - P$x[j] * P$y)) / 2 }
RECT  <- data.frame(x = c(XQ[1], XQ[2], XQ[2], XQ[1]), y = c(YLIM[1], YLIM[1], YLIM[2], YLIM[2]))
below <- function(f) function(x, y) y - ev2(f, x)          # <= 0 means below the boundary
LN    <- list(i = PB$i, Nch = PB$Nch, koff = PB$koff, kon = PB$kon, h = BH, l = BL)

# s[k] = 1 -> the region lies BELOW line k, and below a measurability boundary is the side on which
# that parameter IS measurable. The rates survive exactly when k_off does (no cell carries k_on
# without it) and the amplitude survives exactly when i does (none carries N_ch without it), so the
# whole partition is s[1] and s[3]. k_on and s[2] play no part in it.
regions <- function(hatch_bad) do.call(rbind, lapply(0:(2^length(LN) - 1), function(m) {
  s <- as.integer(intToBits(m))[seq_along(LN)]
  lseok <- s[6] == 0
  yld <- if (s[3] == 0) "none" else if (s[1] == 1) "amp" else if (lseok) "lse" else "rate"
  col <- if (s[5] == 1 && !hatch_bad) "bad" else yld
  P <- RECT
  for (k in seq_along(LN)) P <- clip1(P, local({ g <- below(LN[[k]]); sk <- s[k]
    if (sk == 1) g else function(x, y) -g(x, y) }))
  if (area(P) < 1e-8) return(NULL)
  transform(P, grp = m, fill = PAL[[col]])
}))

# the two textures. Both are line screens, so neither costs a colour; they differ in ink, angle and
# pitch, and the only place they could meet is the bottom of the last simulated column.
lines_in <- function(px, py, angle_deg, spacing) {
  th <- angle_deg * pi / 180
  rx <-  cos(th) * px + sin(th) * py; ry <- -sin(th) * px + cos(th) * py
  n <- length(px); out <- list()
  for (L in seq(min(ry), max(ry), by = spacing)) {
    xs <- numeric(0)
    for (i in seq_len(n)) { j <- if (i == n) 1L else i + 1L
      if ((ry[i] - L) * (ry[j] - L) < 0) {
        t <- (L - ry[i]) / (ry[j] - ry[i]); xs <- c(xs, rx[i] + t * (rx[j] - rx[i])) } }
    xs <- sort(xs)
    if (length(xs) >= 2) for (k in seq(1, length(xs) - 1, by = 2))
      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        x = cos(th)*xs[k] - sin(th)*L, y = sin(th)*xs[k] + cos(th)*L,
        xend = cos(th)*xs[k+1] - sin(th)*L, yend = sin(th)*xs[k+1] + cos(th)*L)
  }
  if (!length(out)) NULL else do.call(rbind, out)
}
BADP  <- clip1(RECT, below(BH))                                    # the dishonest corner
BADH  <- lines_in(BADP$x, BADP$y, 45, 0.155)
EXTRA <- lines_in(c(XSIM, XQ[2], XQ[2], XSIM), c(YLIM[1], YLIM[1], YLIM[2], YLIM[2]), -45, 0.78)

YD <- function(v) log10(v * 10)          # dimensionless noise -> the data's own units
# panel is about 6.30 x 5.25 in inside a 7.0 x 5.9 in device
ASPECT <- (diff(XQ) / diff(YLIM)) * (5.25 / 6.30)
# TWO CLASSES OF INLINE LABEL, drawn differently because they name two different kinds of statement.
# A PARAMETER label names a thin black line and is set the same way: dark text on plain white, no
# edge. An ALGORITHM label names a honesty boundary, which is drawn white cased in dark -- a double
# line -- so the label repeats that: a white bar with a dark edge around it, bold. The label then
# looks like a piece of the line it belongs to, and no reader has to be told which is which.
# (label.size is silently IGNORED by annotate("label") in ggplot2 >= 3.5 -- it warns and applies the
# 0.25 default -- so the edge has to be set through linewidth, which is why AK's labels all carried
# a faint box nobody asked for.)
online <- function(f, x, txt, dy = 0.22, pt = 8) {
  lx <- log10(x)
  annotate("label", x = lx, y = ev2(f, lx) + dy, label = txt, size = PT(pt), colour = "grey5",
           angle = atan(f$co[2] * ASPECT) * 180 / pi, hjust = .5, parse = TRUE,
           fill = "white", alpha = .85, linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(.9, "pt"))
}
onalgo <- function(f, x, txt, dy = 0.22, pt = 8) {
  lx <- log10(x)
  annotate("label", x = lx, y = ev2(f, lx) + dy, label = txt, size = PT(pt), colour = "grey20",
           angle = atan(f$co[2] * ASPECT) * 180 / pi, hjust = .5, fontface = "bold",
           fill = "white", linewidth = .45, label.r = unit(0, "pt"),
           label.padding = unit(1.5, "pt"))
}

# ---- footprint edges moved off the simulated columns --------------------------------------------
# The two small footprints ended exactly on N_ch 10 and 20, which are also two of the columns the
# sweep was run at, so their vertical edges ran through a line of cells and the cells read as beads
# threaded on the box. Moved to 8 and 18. READ BEFORE KEEPING THIS: whole cell's edges are DERIVED
# in figure_7.Rmd, not chosen -- 20 = 100 pA / (10 pA x 0.5) and 1e4 = 5 nA / (1 pA x 0.5), so they
# encode Imin and Imax rather than a guess -- and nudging them means the drawn box no longer states
# those two currents. The right edge costs a second thing: at 1e4 the footprint ended exactly where
# the simulations end, so whole cell was entirely covered by measured cells; at 2e4 it crosses into
# the veiled half. Set NUDGE <- FALSE to get the derived footprints back. The legibility problem it
# solves can also be solved by giving the cells a white halo, which costs no number at all.
NUDGE <- FALSE
if (NUDGE) {
  NEW <- list("excised outside-out patch" = c(8, 300),
              "whole cell"                = c(18, 2e4),
              "oocyte, two-electrode"     = c(1e5, 5e7))
  POLYC <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(PREP)), function(k) {
    p <- PREP[k, ]; e <- NEW[[p$name]]
    xs <- seq(log10(e[1]), log10(e[2]), length.out = 160); N <- 10^xs
    itop <- pmax(I_LO, p$Imin / (N * POPEN))   # few channels have to be big ones
    ibot <- pmin(I_HI, p$Imax / (N * POPEN))   # many channels have to be small ones
    data.frame(name = p$name, x = c(xs, rev(xs)),
               y = pmin(pmax(c(log10(lbl(p$S_hi, p$tau_lo, itop)),
                               rev(log10(lbl(p$S_lo, p$tau_hi, ibot)))), YLIM[1]), YLIM[2]))
  }))
  cat("\nfootprint edges drawn at:", paste(sapply(names(NEW), function(n)
      sprintf("%s %g-%g", n, NEW[[n]][1], NEW[[n]][2])), collapse = "; "), "\n")
}

# LINE CODING. White over a dark casing = a statement about an ALGORITHM's error bar; plain black =
# a statement about whether a PARAMETER can be measured. Solid over the N_ch span where that
# boundary's own crossings were measured, dashed where the fit is carried beyond them.
seg3 <- function(f, cap = NULL) {
  lo <- max(f$lo, XQ[1]); hi <- min(f$hi, XQ[2])
  y <- function(d) { d$y <- ev2(f, d$x); if (!is.null(cap)) d$y <- pmin(d$y, ev2(cap, d$x)); d }
  out <- rbind(if (lo > XQ[1] + 1e-9) data.frame(x = seq(XQ[1], lo, length.out = 60), s = "L") else NULL,
               if (hi < XQ[2] - 1e-9) data.frame(x = seq(hi, XQ[2], length.out = 200), s = "R") else NULL)
  list(ins = y(data.frame(x = seq(lo, hi, length.out = 200))),
       out = if (is.null(out)) NULL else y(out))
}
measur <- function(f, cap = NULL) { p <- seg3(f, cap)
  list(geom_line(data = p$ins, aes(x, y), colour = "grey5", linewidth = .45),
       if (!is.null(p$out)) geom_line(data = p$out, aes(x, y, group = s), colour = "grey5",
                                      linewidth = .45, linetype = "22") else NULL) }
honesty <- function(f) { p <- seg3(f)
  list(geom_line(data = p$ins, aes(x, y), colour = "grey25", linewidth = 1.6),
       geom_line(data = p$ins, aes(x, y), colour = "white",  linewidth = 1.05),
       # thinner outside the fit: the IR-honesty line is fitted over one decade and drawn over
       # seven, so at full weight it is the loudest mark in the panel and the least supported
       if (!is.null(p$out)) list(
         geom_line(data = p$out, aes(x, y, group = s), colour = "grey25", linewidth = 1.0,
                   linetype = "42"),
         geom_line(data = p$out, aes(x, y, group = s), colour = "white", linewidth = .6,
                   linetype = "42")) else NULL) }
CROSS <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(PB), function(p)
  setNames(transform(PB[[p]]$pts[, c("lx","c")], par = p), c("x","y","par"))))

# where each preparation's tab hangs: an N_ch chosen so the three do not collide, and the y taken
# from that footprint's OWN top edge (POLY is built top-run first, then the floor reversed), so the
# tab is attached to the box rather than floating inside it.
# TEVC = two-electrode voltage clamp, which is what PREP's "oocyte, two-electrode" row is; it is
# standard in the field's literature, so the acronym earns its place on a tab this size, but it has
# to be spelled out in the caption. The patch row is named for its ORIENTATION rather than for being
# excised, because the whole map assumes an agonist concentration jump and only an outside-out patch
# puts the extracellular face in the bath: "excised patch" would take in inside-out, which cannot run
# the experiment being mapped. The tabs hang where the name still fits inside its own footprint --
# N_ch 25 for the patch, whose top edge is flat from N_ch 20 on, so the height does not move. That
# one is set over two lines: on one it is 1.12 decades wide against a 1.48-decade footprint, so it
# arrives within a hair of the box's own right edge whatever N_ch it hangs from.
# hj = 0 hangs the tab from the top edge running rightwards, hj = 1 hangs it from the top RIGHT
# corner running leftwards. The patch tab takes the corner: at 1.12 decades against a 1.48-decade
# footprint it fits on one line only if it is anchored to an edge, and the corner is the one part of
# that box with no boundary line crossing it -- hung on the left it landed among k_on, N_ch and the
# IR label. It still covers the three cells on the noise = 0.2 row inside its own span; that is the
# cheapest thing available to cover there, and cheaper than covering a line.
PTAB <- do.call(rbind, lapply(list(c("excised outside-out patch", "outside-out patch", "3.0e2", "1"),
                                   c("whole cell",                "whole cell",        "3.5e2", "0"),
                                   c("oocyte, two-electrode",     "oocyte, TEVC",      "1.15e5","0")),
  function(z) { d <- POLYC[POLYC$name == z[1], ]; top <- d[seq_len(nrow(d) / 2), ]
    data.frame(lab = z[2], hj = as.numeric(z[4]), lx = log10(as.numeric(z[3])),
               ly = approx(top$x, top$y, xout = log10(as.numeric(z[3])))$y - .04) }))

# Does the DRAWN partition agree with the cells it was fitted from? Every earlier revision drew
# fitted lines over measured cells and never asked. Classify each cell twice, once from its own
# measurements and once from the four fitted lines, and count the disagreements.
CHK <- CELL %>% mutate(lx = log10(nch), ly = log10(noise)) %>%
  left_join(irse %>% filter(D == DREF, par %in% c("i","koff")) %>%
              mutate(ok = se < TH) %>% select(par, nch, noise, ok) %>%
              tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = par, values_from = ok), by = c("nch","noise")) %>%
  mutate(cell = case_when(irbad == 1 ~ "bad", !koff ~ "none", i ~ "amp",
                          !is.na(l) & l < log(1.15) ~ "lse", TRUE ~ "rate"),
         drawn = case_when(ly < ev2(BH, lx) ~ "bad", ly > ev2(PB$koff, lx) ~ "none",
                           ly < ev2(PB$i, lx) ~ "amp",
                           ly > ev2(BL, lx) ~ "lse", TRUE ~ "rate"))
cat(sprintf("\npartition check: %d of %d cells disagree with the fitted lines\n",
            sum(CHK$cell != CHK$drawn), nrow(CHK)))
print(table(cell = CHK$cell, drawn = CHK$drawn))
print(as.data.frame(CHK %>% filter(cell != drawn) %>% arrange(nch, noise) %>%
                    select(nch, noise, cell, drawn)))

for (HATCH_BAD in c(TRUE, FALSE)) {

# ---- the key. One swatch column, because the tool axis is no longer a second dimension of the
# fill: it is the ORDER of the rows. Laid out on an explicit cursor in text lines rather than on a
# row count, since the blocks are 1, 2 and 5 lines tall and a uniform row pitch either overlaps them
# or wastes half the box. LH is one 7 pt line measured in y units: the panel is 5.25 in over
# diff(YLIM) decades, so a decade is 0.536 in and 9 pt of leading is 0.233 of one.
LH  <- 0.235
KX  <- c(log10(1.05e5), XQ[2] - .05)
kcx <- KX[1] + diff(KX) * .075; ktx <- KX[1] + diff(KX) * .165
kw  <- diff(KX) * .048; kh <- LH * .62
kx0 <- kcx - kw; kx1 <- kcx + kw + diff(KX) * .06
Y <- local({ y <- 0; f <- function(n, gap = 0) { y <<- y - gap - LH * n / 2
                                                 v <- y; y <<- y - LH * n / 2; v }
             list(next_ = f, used = function() -y) })
y_title <- Y$next_(1, .30)
y_rows  <- c(Y$next_(1, .18), Y$next_(1, .10), Y$next_(1, .10), Y$next_(1, .10), Y$next_(1, .10))
y_note  <- Y$next_(1, .16)
y_line1 <- Y$next_(2, .18)
y_line2 <- Y$next_(2, .10)
y_gloss <- Y$next_(1, .16)
# anchored from the FLOOR, not from a chosen top: a box sized from the top runs off the bottom of
# the panel and ggplot then drops the whole rect, silently, leaving the key with no background.
KY  <- c(YLIM[1] + .02, 0); KY[2] <- KY[1] + Y$used() + .12
kr  <- function(v) KY[2] + v
# ROW ORDER IS THE PANEL'S OWN VERTICAL ORDER, top to bottom: the key is a section through the map,
# its first row the region at the top of the panel and its last the one at the bottom. Listing them
# in the order a column is crossed going UP matches the sequence but reverses the direction, so the
# reader has to flip between key and map; this way the two are read the same way round.
FILLS <- c(PAL[["none"]], PAL[["lse"]], PAL[["rate"]], PAL[["amp"]],
           if (HATCH_BAD) PAL[["amp"]] else PAL[["bad"]])
KEY <- list(
  # opaque, not alpha .95: at 95% the white veil stripes behind still print as faint bands
  annotate("rect", xmin = KX[1], xmax = KX[2], ymin = KY[1], ymax = KY[2],
           fill = "white", colour = "grey70", linewidth = .25),
  annotate("text", x = kx0, y = kr(y_title), hjust = 0, size = PT(7.5), colour = "grey30",
                      # No second person. Published prose in the manuscript uses "you" zero times (the two hits
           # in 00_abstract.tex are both inside % comments), and no other caption in the set has it,
           # so a key written at the reader would be the one place in the paper that does.
           fontface = "italic", label = "what to use, and what it recovers"),
  annotate("rect", xmin = kcx - kw, xmax = kcx + kw, ymin = kr(y_rows) - kh,
           ymax = kr(y_rows) + kh, fill = FILLS, colour = "grey70", linewidth = .2),
  # the dishonest corner keeps its hatch in the key when it has one on the map
  if (HATCH_BAD) geom_segment(data = lines_in(
      c(kcx-kw, kcx+kw, kcx+kw, kcx-kw),
      c(kr(y_rows[5])-kh, kr(y_rows[5])-kh, kr(y_rows[5])+kh, kr(y_rows[5])+kh), 45, .075),
      aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend), colour = "grey15", linewidth = .22,
      inherit.aes = FALSE) else NULL,
  # PRESCRIPTIVE, not descriptive: this is a usage map, so the rows say what to do and the thing
  # that varies is the first word. Three of the five reading "use MacroIR" is the argument and not a
  # collapse of it -- at a glance the likelihood is needed almost everywhere. Two of the rows were
  # arrived at against my own first objection and are worth recording:
  #   AMBER. "use ILSE" is right, not merely permitted. Both methods recover the rates there and both
  #   are calibrated, and the widths are the same: over the 32 cells where both were run the ratio
  #   of the corrected standard error, ILSE over IR, has median 1.04 on k_off and 1.01 on k_on, and
  #   in two of the six rate entries of the three amber cells ILSE is the TIGHTER of the two. Same
  #   answer, same interval, cheaper method. This is Figure 4's corrected covariance and the
  #   information budget: the rates live in the shape of the deterministic transient.
  #   VIOLET. "use MacroIR but do not trust the calibration" tells the reader to use a method and
  #   distrust it without saying what to do instead. What is wrong there is the REPORTED interval,
  #   so that is what the row names. The estimate itself is not what the diagnostic condemns.
  # "often all four": 11 of the 63 cells in the first region carry only k_off and the conductance,
  # so naming the full four would be false over a sixth of it. The two thin lines inside the region
  # are where the other two go, and the caption carries the subset table.
  annotate("text", x = ktx, y = kr(y_rows), hjust = 0, size = PT(7.5), colour = "grey25",
           parse = TRUE,
           # Two of these were written for the old row order and stopped parsing when it changed.
           # "calibrated here TOO" pointed at a MacroIR row that used to sit above it and now sits
           # below, so the antecedent is gone and the row is made self-contained. In exchange the
           # new order earns an anaphora the old one could not have: the conductance row now sits
           # directly under the rates row, so "i as well" has something to be as well AS, which is
           # how the rows were first drafted.
           label = c("'nothing measurable'",
                     "'use ILSE:  calibrated here, and cheaper'",
                     "'use MacroIR:  the rates, calibrated'",
                     "'use MacroIR:'~italic(i)~'as well, often all four'",
                     "'use MacroIR, but not its reported interval'")),
  # WHY the first row belongs to one method only, stated as a fact about the method and nothing
  # more. It used to carry a second clause, "so in the top row it is not a candidate at all", which
  # was cut: "top row" is the key's first row but the MAP's lowest region, and read as the map it
  # says the opposite of the amber region, where least squares is an honest option. The reader who
  # needs the inference has the row above; the caption spells it out.
  annotate("text", x = kx0, y = kr(y_note), hjust = 0, size = PT(7), colour = "grey30",
           fontface = "italic",
           label = "ILSE holds i fixed and cannot separate N_ch from it"),
  # the two line classes, explained once here instead of twice on the map
  annotate("rect", xmin = kx0 - .02, xmax = kx1 + .02, ymin = kr(y_line1) - kh*.9,
           ymax = kr(y_line1) + kh*.9, fill = PAL[["rate"]], colour = NA),
  annotate("segment", x = kx0, xend = kx1, y = kr(y_line1), yend = kr(y_line1),
           colour = "grey25", linewidth = 1.6),
  annotate("segment", x = kx0, xend = kx1, y = kr(y_line1), yend = kr(y_line1),
           colour = "white", linewidth = 1.05),
  annotate("segment", x = kx0, xend = (kx0 + kx1)/2, y = kr(y_line2), yend = kr(y_line2),
           colour = "grey5", linewidth = .45),
  annotate("segment", x = (kx0 + kx1)/2, xend = kx1, y = kr(y_line2), yend = kr(y_line2),
           colour = "grey5", linewidth = .45, linetype = "22"),
  annotate("point", x = (kx0 + kx1)/2, y = kr(y_line2), size = 1.1, shape = 21,
           fill = "white", colour = "grey5", stroke = .35),
  annotate("text", x = kx1 + .10, y = c(kr(y_line1), kr(y_line2)), hjust = 0, size = PT(7),
           colour = "grey25", lineheight = .95,
           label = c("that interval becomes calibrated\n(information distortion = 1.15)",
                     "that parameter stops being measurable\n(standard error = a factor of 2)")),
  annotate("text", x = kx0, y = kr(y_gloss), hjust = 0, size = PT(7), colour = "grey30",
           label = "IR = MacroIR;  ILSE = classical least squares."))

gq <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = regions(HATCH_BAD), aes(x, y, group = grp, fill = fill, colour = fill),
               linewidth = .12) +
  scale_fill_identity() + scale_colour_identity() +
  (if (HATCH_BAD) geom_segment(data = BADH, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
                               colour = "grey15", linewidth = .28, inherit.aes = FALSE) else NULL) +
  # past the last simulated column there is nothing but the fits, so the fills are veiled
  geom_segment(data = EXTRA, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
               colour = "white", linewidth = .55, alpha = .5, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  measur(PB$i) + measur(PB$koff) + measur(PB$kon) + measur(PB$Nch, cap = PB$i) +
  honesty(BL) + honesty(BH) +
  geom_point(data = CROSS, aes(x, y), size = 1.1, shape = 21, fill = "white",
             colour = "grey5", stroke = .35) +
  # THE THREE PREPARATIONS ARE A DIFFERENT KIND OF OBJECT from everything else in the panel: they
  # are where real experiments sit, not something the sweep measured. In AK they were drawn in the
  # same language as the diagnostics -- thin dark outline, white label box, same size -- so "patch"
  # and "k_off" read as the same class of thing. Here they get their own: a heavier outline, and a
  # solid tab hung from the box's own top edge with the name reversed out of it. Reversed on solid
  # is the exact inverse of the boundary labels (dark on white), which is the cheapest way to say
  # "different layer" without spending a colour or a line style that already means something.
  geom_polygon(data = POLYC, aes(x, y, group = name), fill = NA, colour = "grey5",
               linewidth = .8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  lapply(c(0, 1), function(h) geom_label(data = PTAB[PTAB$hj == h, ],
             aes(x = lx, y = ly, label = lab), size = PT(7.5), colour = "white",
             fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey5", linewidth = 0,
             label.padding = unit(1.8, "pt"), hjust = h, vjust = 1)) +
  # a thin white ring, so a cell still reads as a cell where a footprint edge runs through its
  # column. That collision is what the footprint edges were nudged off, and the ring solves it
  # without moving a number: two of those edges are DERIVED (whole cell 20 = 100 pA / (10 pA x 0.5)
  # and 1e4 = 5 nA / (1 pA x 0.5)), so a caption cannot state them and the drawing show something
  # else. NUDGE is kept for comparison but is off.
  geom_point(data = CELL %>% mutate(x = log10(nch), y = log10(noise)), aes(x, y),
             size = .95, shape = 21, fill = "grey5", colour = "white", stroke = .28) +
  # THE EDGE OF THE VEIL, drawn last of the map marks so the preparation boxes cannot bury it: the
  # whole-cell footprint happens to end at exactly N_ch 1e4, so its heavy edge was sitting on top of
  # this line for the bottom third of the panel. Pure white, no casing, matching the veil stripes it
  # bounds -- the honesty lines are white CASED IN DARK, so the two never read as the same mark.
  # The caption hangs off the line itself rather than floating in the middle of the veiled half.
  annotate("segment", x = XSIM, xend = XSIM, y = YLIM[1], yend = YLIM[2],
           colour = "white", linewidth = 1.0, linetype = "42") +
  annotate("segment", x = XSIM, xend = XSIM + .60, y = YLIM[2] - .42, yend = YLIM[2] - .42,
           colour = "white", linewidth = .9) +
  # italic grey on white, which is this figure's voice for an editorial note (the key's own notes are
  # set the same way): not bold-on-solid, which now means a preparation, and not a plain white box,
  # which now means a parameter. Reversed white type failed anyway -- half the sentence lands on the
  # mid green and stops being legible.
  annotate("label", x = XSIM + .55, y = YLIM[2] - .42, hjust = 0, size = PT(7.5), colour = "grey20",
           fontface = "italic", label = "no simulations beyond here", fill = "white",
           linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(1.4, "pt")) +
  # the inline labels last of all, so nothing crosses them
  online(PB$i,    2.2e2, "italic(i)",  .20) +
  online(PB$Nch,  1.5e3, "N[ch]",    -.30) +
  online(PB$koff, 3.0e1, "k[off]",     .20) +
  online(PB$kon,  1.2e2, "k[on]",      .20) +
  onalgo(BL, 6.0e3, "ILSE", .30, 8) +
  onalgo(BH, 45,    "IR",  .34, 8) +
  KEY +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = log10(10^(1:8)),
                     labels = lapply(1:8, function(e) if (e == 1) "10" else bquote(10^.(e))),
                     limits = XQ, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = log10(10^(-2:7)),
                     labels = lapply((-2:7) - 1, function(e)
                       if (e >= -2 && e <= 1) format(10^e, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
                       else bquote(10^.(e))),
                     limits = YLIM, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = expression(N[ch]), y = "dimensionless instrumental noise") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 9.5), axis.text = element_text(size = 8),
        plot.margin = margin(4, 5, 2, 4))

# the hatch sibling is the BODY FIGURE since 2026-08-26; the purple override is the alternative
f <- if (HATCH_BAD) "Figure_7_hatch" else "Figure_7"
ggsave(paste0(f, ".pdf"), gq, width = 7.0, height = 5.9, device = cairo_pdf)
ggsave(paste0(f, ".png"), gq, width = 7.0, height = 5.9, dpi = 140)
if (!HATCH_BAD) print(gq)
}
```
